clue.text: Glasses broken initially, if pubs open late

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word broken

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: pubs that open late here lose their opening letter, starting one place in

parts.note: locals are the pubs people use near home

explanation.surface: Someone's glasses got smashed while waiting for pubs with late licences to open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open late' is a trimming signal: LOCALS starts late, losing its L to give OCALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bifocals are spectacles with lenses split for near and distance vision.

clue.text: Live with a North European — a tall, thin person

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: Someone lives with a lanky man from northern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Beanpole is an informal word for a very tall, skinny person.

clue.text: Scent identified in a Continental newspaper?

indicators.note: in means the paper sits inside the country

parts.note: France is a country on the Continent, as Britons call mainland Europe
a rag is a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: A perfume is mentioned in a European newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrance is a pleasant smell or perfume.

clue.text: Boat for a small number — 30 at the outside

indicators.note: at the outside means the cross-referenced letters sit around the rest

parts.note: the answer to 30 across, with civil, gives CE for civil engineer
No is the short form of number

explanation.surface: A boat for a few people, with thirty at most.
explanation.walkthrough: '30' points to the answer of 30 across, abbreviated as in CE, civil engineer; 'at the outside' wraps it round A NO.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a light narrow boat paddled by hand.

clue.text: Shakespearean tale teller — a good person to thrash

parts.note: Charles Lamb wrote Tales from Shakespeare with his sister Mary
St, short for saint, is a good person

explanation.surface: A narrator of Shakespeare stories turns out to be a decent person worth beating.
explanation.definitionFit: To lambast is to beat severely or berate harshly.

clue.text: Pass end of avenue by mistake

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the word avenue

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or mistake

explanation.surface: Someone drives past the end of the avenue in error.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to pass or elapse, both meaning go by.

clue.text: Half-hearted communication about frozen food in the city

indicators.note: about means the trimmed word goes round the frozen food
half-hearted removes half of the middle pair of letters in the word

parts.note: a letter is a written communication
ices are frozen desserts

explanation.surface: A lukewarm message about frozen meals reaches the city.
explanation.walkthrough: LETTER's heart is TT; 'Half-hearted' drops one T to give LETER, which goes 'about' ICES.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester is a city in the English East Midlands.

clue.text: Something incriminating concealed in a factory

explanation.surface: Evidence has been hidden in a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant is evidence secretly placed to frame someone, and also an industrial works.

clue.text: Regularly install an archdeacon in the diocese

indicators.note: install means placing the cleric inside the diocese

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and diocese in Cambridgeshire
Ven, short for Venerable, is an archdeacon's title

explanation.surface: An archdeacon is routinely installed in the diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Evenly means at a steady, uniform rate, as regularly does.

clue.text: Cakes once cooked on board ship

indicators.note: on board means the letters go inside the ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of once are worked over into a new form

explanation.surface: Cakes were once baked on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Scones are small baked cakes, often served with jam and cream.

clue.text: A trendy state invading on a further occasion

indicators.note: invading signals one piece pushing its way inside the others

parts.note: in means fashionable
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A fashionable nation invades a neighbour once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on a further occasion is doing it once more.

clue.text: One friend absorbed in another's intrigue

indicators.note: absorbed in means one friend's word is taken inside the other's

parts.note: mate is another word for friend
china, from rhyming slang china plate = mate, means friend

explanation.surface: One friend gets caught up in another's scheming.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with mate, so a CHINA is a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: To machinate is to plot or scheme, the verb sense of intrigue.

clue.text: Cut-back reduced girl's ceramic work

indicators.note: back sends the word for cut the other way round

parts.note: to crop is to cut short

indicators.note: reduced trims the last letter off the girl's name

parts.note: Elaine is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl's pottery is downsized after budget cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CROP into PORC; 'reduced' cuts ELAINE to ELAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain is fine china, the material of much ceramic ware.

clue.text: Praise former partner before setback

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
a set is a lot, and lot turned back reads tol

explanation.surface: Someone praises their ex before suffering a reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' is read as set (LOT) going back, giving TOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to laud or speak highly of.

clue.text: Blocked relief until new commander intervened

indicators.note: intervened means the commander comes between the shuffled letters
new tells us the word until is remade in a fresh order

parts.note: OC stands for Officer Commanding

explanation.surface: Relief from a blockade was delayed until a new commander stepped in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns UNTIL into LINUT; 'intervened' puts OC, Officer Commanding, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A linocut is a relief print made from a carved block of linoleum.

clue.text: American president's endlessly ingenious tract

indicators.note: endlessly drops the final letter of the word for ingenious

parts.note: clever means ingenious
land is a tract of ground

explanation.surface: A US president's clever pamphlet goes on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts CLEVER to CLEVE; the 's is 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Grover Cleveland was the 22nd and 24th US president.

clue.text: The bench in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A judge's bench is located in North Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: A settle is a high-backed wooden bench; Settle is also a market town in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A settle is a long wooden seat with a high back, and Settle is a Yorkshire Dales town.

clue.text: Vital cure possibly producing a high income

indicators.note: possibly hints that the words vital cure may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A vital cure might make a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucrative means profitable, yielding plenty of money.

clue.text: A base on the river for trainers, perhaps

indicators.note: on means one piece sits upon the other in this down clue

parts.note: a foot is a base, as at the foot of a hill
the Wear is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: A base by the river for those who coach, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trainers' is sports shoes here, not coaches; the definition by example is flagged by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainers are sports shoes, an example of shoes and boots in general.

clue.text: Advance Elizabeth Gaskell originally accepted for a story

indicators.note: accepted means the initials are taken inside the word for advance

parts.note: to advance money is to lend it

indicators.note: originally picks the opening letters of Elizabeth and Gaskell

explanation.surface: A loan to the novelist Elizabeth Gaskell was originally granted for a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional tale or myth.

clue.text: Notes collected in the twenties, say

definitions.text: Notes collected in the twenties, say

parts.words: Notes collected in the twenties, say
parts.note: musical notes gathered together spell out a span of ten years, of which the twenties is one

explanation.surface: Musical notes gathered in the 1920s.
explanation.walkthrough: D, E, C, A, D and E are all names of musical notes, so the notes 'collected' spell the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The twenties are an example of a ten-year period.

clue.text: Hot wind thus enveloping huge bird with oxygen

indicators.note: enveloping means the Latin word wraps around the bird

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as exact
the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A hot wind sweeps over a giant bird, bringing oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot Saharan wind blowing into southern Europe.

clue.text: Pouch for poor parson? About right

indicators.note: About means the reworked letters go round the abbreviation for right
poor suggests the word parson is in bad shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A purse for an impoverished clergyman? That's about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' turns PARSON into SPORAN, which goes 'About' R.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporran is the pouch worn at the front of a Scottish kilt.

clue.text: Books support objection raised about river fish

indicators.note: support means the books sit underneath in this down clue
about means the turned word goes around the river
raised in a down clue means the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: Books bolster a raised objection about a river fish.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' reads upwards and 'support' puts the books at the bottom; OT is the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The turbot is a large flatfish of European waters.

clue.text: Russian tsar's edict — and this kingdom's. it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the possessive is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: UK's is the possessive of the United Kingdom, this kingdom for a British paper

explanation.surface: A decree issued by a Russian tsar, and also one issued by Britain, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A ukase was an imperial Russian decree with the force of law.

clue.text: One's surrounded by drink in the passage

indicators.note: surrounded by means the first piece lies inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink, a kind of beer
I is one, and the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Someone is ringed by drinks in the corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: One's is read as I plus 's (is), giving IS.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats.

clue.text: Vexed worker consumes a single roll

indicators.note: consumes means the pieces swallow the single letter

parts.note: cross means annoyed or vexed
I is the Roman numeral one
the ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: An angry labourer eats a lone bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vexed' looks like a description of the worker, but it gives its own synonym; the single letter goes inside that, not inside the worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A croissant is a crescent-shaped flaky breakfast pastry.

clue.text: 28 ordered out of this inn

indicators.note: ordered out signals letters put out of their order

parts.note: the answer to 28 across supplies these letters

explanation.surface: Someone is ordered out of this inn.
explanation.walkthrough: '28' is the answer to 28 across; rearranged it gives the inn.
explanation.definitionFit: A serai is a caravanserai, a travellers' inn in the East.

clue.text: Fellow in Derby uneasily looking on

indicators.note: in places the fellow inside the reshuffled town name
uneasily suggests the letters of Derby are restless and rearranged

parts.note: Stan is a man's name, hence any fellow

explanation.surface: A man at Derby watches nervously from the sidelines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uneasily' turns DERBY into BYDER; 'in' puts STAN in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bystander is an onlooker who is present but not taking part.

clue.text: Put up beams, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken, matching another in sound

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Builders erect roof beams.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift it or put it up.

clue.text: Like country gentry or the border river?

explanation.surface: Is it like the landed classes, or like a river on the Scottish border?
explanation.walkthrough: Country gentry wear tweeds; the Tweed is the river along the Scottish-English border, so the question mark invites 'Tweed-y'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweedy describes the hearty rural upper class in tweed jackets, and whimsically anything resembling the River Tweed.

clue.text: An artful contriver, though possibly civil

explanation.surface: A cunning schemer, though perhaps a polite one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'civil' looks like 'polite', but it describes the profession: civil, mechanical and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cleverly arranges events is said to manipulate them, and a civil professional builds roads and bridges.
